cards.design_implication: If modeling SMBH binary populations as the source of the gravitational-wave background, ensure that the model architecture can accommodate variations in amplitude and spectral shape to match current measurement precisions.
does_not_establish: A definitive causal link between SMBH binaries and the GWB.
Specific sampling strategies, eligibility criteria, or statistical methods used to validate the models.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We show that astrophysically motivated models of SMBH binary populations are able to reproduce both the amplitude and shape of the observed low-frequency gravitational-wave spectrum.
limitations: This claim is derived from an abstract and does not specify the exact numerical parameters or detailed model structures used.
The text notes that multiple model variations can reproduce the spectrum, implying a lack of unique mechanistic resolution at this stage.
cards.statement: Astrophysically motivated models of supermassive black hole (SMBH) binary populations are able to reproduce the amplitude and shape of the observed low-frequency gravitational-wave spectrum.

cards.design_implication: When designing future simulations or observational analyses of the GWB, account for the tension between standard astrophysical expectations and the observed amplitude by exploring parameter spaces that may include extreme values or non-standard assumptions.
does_not_establish: The specific physical mechanisms causing the deviation from standard expectations.
Control implementations or instrument calibration details.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Additionally, while reasonable parameters are able to reproduce the 15 yr observations, the implied GWB amplitude necessitates either a large number of parameters to be at the edges of expected values or a small number of parameters to be notably different from standard expectations.
limitations: The excerpt describes a tension in the current data model but does not define what constitutes 'standard expectations' or the specific parameter edges.
